technologies.name: Natural Fire
technologies.description: A lightning-struck tree, still smouldering. You keep the embers alive, and they keep giving off heat — your very first source of Energy.

technologies.name: Controlled Fire
technologies.description: A hearth you can light at will, rather than one you happen to find. Warmth, light, and the first fuel you burn on purpose.

technologies.name: Cooking
technologies.description: Cooked food yields more calories, freeing time for tool-making and ideas.

technologies.name: Charcoal Kiln
technologies.description: Slow-burned wood yields a hotter, more portable fuel — civilization's first fuel stockpile.

technologies.name: Pottery
technologies.description: Fired clay vessels let surplus food be stored — the seed of permanent settlement.

technologies.name: Metalworking
technologies.description: Hot enough fires can shape metal. A new material age begins.

technologies.name: Bronze Smelting
technologies.description: Alloying copper and tin produces tools and weapons far tougher than stone.

technologies.name: Iron Smelting
technologies.description: Hotter furnaces smelt iron — stronger, cheaper, and everywhere underfoot.

technologies.name: The Wheel
technologies.description: Everything you already do, done with less effort. +25% to all production.

technologies.name: Early Agriculture
technologies.description: Deliberately planting and storing grain ends the nomadic era for good.

technologies.name: Farming
technologies.description: Cleared and tilled fields feed more mouths than foraging ever could.

technologies.name: Animal Domestication
technologies.description: Herded livestock provide labor, meat, and milk — plus a lot of digestive methane.

technologies.name: Steam Engine
technologies.description: Boiling water under pressure yields mechanical power on demand. The industrial age begins.

technologies.name: Horse & Cart
technologies.description: Domesticated draft animals move goods faster than any human back.

technologies.name: Irrigation
technologies.description: Channeling water to fields turns marginal land productive year-round.

technologies.name: Coal Mining
technologies.description: Deep shafts pull ancient buried carbon out of the ground by the wagonload.

technologies.name: Generator
technologies.description: Spinning a coil in a magnetic field conjures current from motion.

technologies.name: Oil Drilling
technologies.description: Derricks tap ancient buried hydrocarbons — denser energy than coal, easier to move.

technologies.name: Rice Cultivation
technologies.description: Flooded paddies feed empires — and their waterlogged soil breeds methanogenic bacteria by the trillion.

technologies.name: Steam Locomotive
technologies.description: Rail networks haul coal and freight faster than any road ever could.

technologies.name: Oil Refinery
technologies.description: Cracking crude into fuel and feedstock unlocks everything downstream of petroleum.

technologies.name: Steam Vehicle
technologies.description: Self-propelled steam carriages replace the horse on the open road.

technologies.name: Livestock
technologies.description: Industrial-scale herding scales up meat production — and methane output — together.

technologies.name: Factories
technologies.description: Coal-fired machinery under one roof outproduces a hundred workshops.

technologies.name: Coal Power Plant
technologies.description: Burning coal to boil water to spin turbines: the workhorse of the industrial grid.

technologies.name: Concrete
technologies.description: The most-used material on Earth, and one of the most carbon-intensive to produce.

technologies.name: Industrial Chemistry
technologies.description: Systematic chemistry turns raw materials into whatever industry needs next.

technologies.name: Fertilizer
technologies.description: Manure and mineral amendments boost yields beyond what soil alone can sustain.

technologies.name: Steel Production
technologies.description: Bessemer converters turn iron into steel at unprecedented volume.

technologies.name: Cement Production
technologies.description: Roasting limestone into clinker is one of the most carbon-intensive processes in industry.

technologies.name: Grid Electricity
technologies.description: A unified transmission grid lets every factory and home run on demand.

technologies.name: Petrochemicals
technologies.description: Oil becomes plastic, solvent, and synthetic fiber. Petroleum touches everything now.

technologies.name: Natural Gas
technologies.description: Gas burns cleaner than coal, per unit of energy — though it still adds up fast at scale.

technologies.name: Automobile
technologies.description: The internal combustion engine puts a private vehicle within reach of ordinary people.

technologies.name: Ammonia
technologies.description: The Haber-Bosch process fixes nitrogen from thin air at industrial scale, feeding fertilizer plants worldwide.

technologies.name: Synthetic Fertilizer
technologies.description: Haber-Bosch ammonia turns air into fertilizer, feeding billions — and flooding soils with nitrous oxide.

technologies.name: Industrial Furnaces
technologies.description: Ever-hotter furnaces process ore, scrap, and fuel around the clock.

technologies.name: Hydroelectricity
technologies.description: Dammed rivers spin turbines with no combustion at all — clean, steady, huge.

technologies.name: Gas Turbine
technologies.description: Burning natural gas spins a turbine directly — quicker to build, dirtier than hydro.

technologies.name: Mass Production Cars
technologies.description: Assembly lines put a car in every driveway, and exhaust over every street.

technologies.name: Diesel Engine
technologies.description: More torque, more efficiency, more soot — diesel becomes the standard for heavy hauling.

technologies.name: Steel Buildings
technologies.description: Steel frames let buildings rise higher and faster than stone or wood ever allowed.

technologies.name: Industrial Agriculture
technologies.description: Mechanized planting, harvesting, and processing turn farming into heavy industry.

technologies.name: Mass Manufacturing
technologies.description: Standardized parts and assembly lines multiply every factory's output at once.

technologies.name: Coal Industrialization
technologies.description: Double down on cheap, abundant coal. Energy is plentiful; emissions skyrocket.

technologies.name: Nuclear Industrialization
technologies.description: Invest in expensive, complex nuclear infrastructure for enormous clean output.

technologies.name: Fracking
technologies.description: Shattering deep shale releases trapped gas — and lets a fair amount of methane leak straight to the air.

technologies.name: Trucks
technologies.description: Diesel freight trucks connect factories to shelves without needing a railway.

technologies.name: Highways
technologies.description: Paved, limited-access roads let vehicles move faster, farther, and in far greater numbers.

technologies.name: Refrigeration
technologies.description: Mechanical cooling preserves food and comfort alike — using the first synthetic refrigerant gases.

technologies.name: Mega Farms
technologies.description: Horizon-spanning monocultures, fed and fertilized entirely by machine.

technologies.name: Chemical Industry
technologies.description: Industrial-scale chemistry opens doors nature never built.

technologies.name: Nuclear Power
technologies.description: Splitting atoms releases enormous energy with almost no direct emissions.

technologies.name: Offshore Drilling
technologies.description: Platforms far out to sea reach reserves no derrick on land ever could.

technologies.name: Jet Aircraft
technologies.description: Turbojets cross continents in hours, burning fuel at high altitude where it matters more.

technologies.name: Skyscrapers
technologies.description: Kilometer-scale towers pack a city's worth of energy demand onto one city block.

technologies.name: Factory Farming
technologies.description: Livestock raised at industrial density, on an industrial timetable.

technologies.name: Supercritical Coal
technologies.description: Higher pressures and temperatures wring more power from every lump of coal — and more CO₂.

technologies.name: Combined Cycle Gas
technologies.description: Pairing a gas turbine with a steam turbine squeezes far more energy from the same fuel.

technologies.name: Oil Sands
technologies.description: Extracting oil from tar-thick sand takes enormous heat and water — and emits accordingly.

technologies.name: Commercial Aviation
technologies.description: Air travel becomes routine, not remarkable. The skies fill with contrails.

technologies.name: Container Ships
technologies.description: Standardized steel boxes on diesel-burning giants move the world's goods across oceans.

technologies.name: Airports
technologies.description: Runways and terminals sprawl outward to keep pace with air travel demand.

technologies.name: CFCs
technologies.description: Chlorofluorocarbons are cheap, stable, and everywhere — stable enough to drift into the stratosphere and eat ozone.

technologies.name: Mass Electrification
technologies.description: Every corner of civilization now runs on the grid. Output compounds everywhere.

technologies.name: Coal Mega-Mining
technologies.description: Whole mountains are leveled for the coal seams beneath them.

technologies.name: Global Logistics
technologies.description: Trucks, trains, ships, and planes now form one coordinated worldwide supply machine.

technologies.name: Megacities
technologies.description: Tens of millions of people, one continuous urban sprawl, running nonstop.

technologies.name: International Trade
technologies.description: Nations specialize and trade at scale, wiring the world's economies together.

technologies.name: Mega Infrastructure
technologies.description: Nationwide grids, ports, and transit systems bind cities into a single machine.

technologies.name: HFCs
technologies.description: Hydrofluorocarbons replace ozone-eating CFCs — leaving the ozone layer alone, and warming the planet directly instead.

technologies.name: Containerization
technologies.description: Standardized shipping containers make loading and moving goods almost frictionless — so the world moves a lot more of them.

technologies.name: Supersonic Aviation
technologies.description: Breaking the sound barrier for a business flight, at an enormous fuel and emissions premium.

technologies.name: Global Urbanization
technologies.description: More than half the human race now lives in cities built this way. There is no going back.

technologies.name: Global Supply Chains
technologies.description: Parts cross a dozen borders before a product is finished. Efficiency has no geography left.

technologies.name: Industrial Fluorinated Gases
technologies.description: PFCs and SF₆: some of the most potent, most persistent greenhouse gases ever synthesized.

technologies.name: Consumer Economy
technologies.description: Mass production meets mass marketing: an economy built on buying more, replacing sooner, discarding faster.

technologies.name: Computers
technologies.description: Electronic computation replaces rooms full of clerks with a single humming cabinet.

technologies.name: Advanced Chemical Manufacturing
technologies.description: Automated, continuous chemical plants run every reaction in this branch simultaneously, everywhere.

technologies.name: Global Aviation Networks
technologies.description: Hub airports link every major city on the planet with a same-day flight.

technologies.name: 24/7 Manufacturing
technologies.description: Factories across every time zone mean production never actually stops, anywhere, ever.

technologies.name: Internet
technologies.description: A global network lets every computer, factory, and market talk to every other, instantly.

technologies.name: Megacorporations
technologies.description: A handful of firms now operate at the scale of nations, and answer to no single one.

technologies.name: Data Centers
technologies.description: Warehouses of servers run around the clock, drawing enormous power to keep the internet online.

technologies.name: Cloud Computing
technologies.description: Computation-as-a-service means every phone and laptop can now offload work to a distant, power-hungry server farm.

technologies.name: AI
technologies.description: Machine learning models train on oceans of data, accelerating research — and power demand — together.

technologies.name: Mass AI Infrastructure
technologies.description: Entire power grids are now built specifically to feed AI training clusters.

technologies.name: Hyperscale Data Centers
technologies.description: Campuses of data centers the size of small cities, humming continuously, forever.

technologies.name: Advanced Manufacturing
technologies.description: Robotic, self-replicating factories need no rest, no wages, and no limits.

technologies.name: Fusion Power
technologies.description: Thirty years away for a century, and then suddenly not. Limitless clean power arrives — and gets spent, immediately and entirely, on running everything else harder.

technologies.name: Orbital Industry
technologies.description: Factories in orbit promise a cleaner future — powered by an awful lot of rocket fuel to get there.

technologies.name: Space Elevator
technologies.description: A ribbon of carbon from the equator to geostationary orbit. Lifting a tonne off Earth stops being an event and starts being a Tuesday.

technologies.name: Moon Mining
technologies.description: Helium-3 and rare earths from the Moon feed an industry that never once slows down to ask why.

technologies.name: Asteroid Capture
technologies.description: Whole metallic asteroids are nudged into Earth orbit and taken apart. The commodity markets have never been calmer, or the sky busier.

technologies.name: Planetary Industry
technologies.description: Every remaining hectare of the planet's surface is now industrial infrastructure of some kind.

technologies.name: Terraforming Engines
technologies.description: Continent-scale machines built to put the climate back where it was. They run on the same industry that broke it, and they are losing.

technologies.name: Dyson Swarm Prototype
technologies.description: The first panels of a solar-collecting swarm go up. Harvesting a star, warming a planet — a footnote by comparison.

technologies.name: Matrioshka Brain
technologies.description: Nested shells of computation wrapped around the sun, thinking thoughts nobody on the surface can follow. The waste heat alone is a weather system.

technologies.name: Stellar Energy
technologies.description: Your civilization now answers its energy needs with a literal star. Ambition has entirely outrun restraint.
